comment: Which deliberate emitter refusals the conformance matrix is allowed to
publish as `lim`, a tier limit. Issue #1342, issue #1347.
`lim` is read as 'this tier cannot express this construct'. An emitter
can also refuse for a reason that is about the DOCUMENT the corpus built
rather than about the construct under test, and it can refuse because a
stdlib method simply has no arm on that path yet. The matrix has no way
to tell the three apart from the exception alone: all of them arrive as
the tier's own EmitError. Publishing either of the last two as `lim`
understates the tier, in the fail-open direction for a reader deciding
whether revl suits them.
So a refusal is `lim` only if it is written down here, with the reason it
is a capability limit. Anything else is UNCLASSIFIED, and an unclassified
cell stops `--write-readme` and `--check-readme` rather than being
downgraded. `message_prefix` is what makes an entry perishable: the entry
applies only while the emitter still refuses for the reason recorded, so
a rewritten refusal drops back to unclassified instead of inheriting a
judgement made about different words.
The go column's history is the worked example. Issue #1321 (PR #1355)
carried the mixed document the pure path used to drop, which closed 22 of
the 24 cells that were unclassified here. Of the two left, one was never a
capability limit either: `expr/Int32 bitwise` refused with 'unknown stdlib
method: to_int32' because the narrow had an arm on the pure typed-core
path and none in a component method body, while the widen beside it did.
That is a missing arm, so it was implemented rather than classified, and
the cell now executes. Only the arrow below is a real tier limit.

java::method/arrow param binds in method.reason: a declared function type has no nominal target type on the JVM, so the emitter has nothing to emit the lambda against. A capability limit of the tier.

wasm::component/config field.reason: the cordis-wasm runtime has no instantiation-config channel, so a config block has no lowering. A capability limit of the runtime.
wasm::component/config field.message_prefix: C: config blocks are not lowerable

wasm::component/fail (A8).reason: the cordis-wasm runtime has no instantiation-config channel, so a config block has no lowering. The same capability limit as component/config field.
wasm::component/fail (A8).message_prefix: C: config blocks are not lowerable

wasm::component/effect + undo.reason: the host builtin Map.new is not on the cordis-wasm tier. A capability limit of the runtime's builtin set.
wasm::component/effect + undo.message_prefix: C: host builtin 'Map.new' is not available

wasm::component/block effect setup.reason: the host builtin Map.new is not on the cordis-wasm tier. A capability limit of the runtime's builtin set.
wasm::component/block effect setup.message_prefix: C: host builtin 'Map.new' is not available

wasm::method/method-time effect.reason: the host builtin Map.new is not on the cordis-wasm tier. A capability limit of the runtime's builtin set.
wasm::method/method-time effect.message_prefix: C: host builtin 'Map.new' is not available

wasm::method/arrow param binds in method.reason: arrow values have no lowering on this tier. A capability limit.
wasm::method/arrow param binds in method.message_prefix: C.s.f: arrow values are not lowerable

wasm::expr/true division.reason: Float is not in the tier's lowerable value set. A capability limit.

wasm::expr/float equality.reason: Float is not in the tier's lowerable value set. A capability limit.
wasm::expr/float equality.message_prefix: feq: parameter a: type 'Float' is not lowerable

wasm::type/Float service.reason: Float is not in the tier's lowerable value set. A capability limit.
wasm::type/Float service.message_prefix: C: s.f param 'x': type 'Float' is not lowerable

wasm::type/Map service.reason: Map is not in the tier's lowerable value set. A capability limit.
wasm::type/Map service.message_prefix: C: s.f param 'x': type 'Map[Str, Int]' is not lowerable

go::method/arrow param binds in method s.reason: the stc-go component world has no arrow lowering: a general arrow in a component body has no type to render the closure against, so the emitter has nothing to emit it as. A capability limit of the component tier, not a document-shape refusal — it fires the same way on a document that is ONLY a component, with no top-level declaration beside it. The go tier does lower an arrow on the pure typed-core path and in a stream combinator (both have a known item type); the case measured here is the arrow in METHOD scope, which is what the cell claims.
go::method/arrow param binds in method s.message_prefix: arrow is not lowerable in the stc-go component world
